sources.note: Nothing on 重音/stress anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent + page reading). Main variety = Longchuan (Husa, Lajie) [acha1249]: 4 tones (p.16); 联音音变 (三) 弱化: first syllable of a disyllable with rhyme a is weakened to [ə], 'slightly lighter and shorter' (p.22). Dialect chapter (pp.81-98) explicitly describes the Lianghe dialect (襄宋公社关璋话): 34 initials (p.81), no -m/-p codas (p.85), three tones 55/35/31, checked rhymes only on 55 and 31, low-falling open syllables end in a short -ʔ, high-rising tone mostly on the 2nd syllable of disyllables and rare on monosyllables (p.86).
